disclosure.screen_space_ui: cells touched by the bounding rectangles of HUD-camera renderers and canvas graphics with visible alpha carry the unknown bit; actors, hazards and doors wholly under one are not reported (view.window.ui_rects lists the rectangles)
disclosure.unsupported: scenery, background and particles are not reported; menus, map and inventory screens are not reported
disclosure.resolution: 20 px cells on a 960 x 540 screen; the game window is taken as 960 x 540
disclosure.debug: debug_observation.json / observations.jsonl hold global state; plumbing and evaluation only

view.world_units: 1 unit = 1 Unity world unit of the game (the knight's body is about 0.5 x 1.3 units); x right, y up; origin per room; screen x right/y down

legend.unknown: ? outside the game window, or covered by the HUD / a text box; never safe

rules: Walk left/right, jump (the longer the button is held the higher, up to a full jump), strike with the nail left/right/up and, in the air, down.
Enemies and spikes hurt on touch; with no health left the knight dies and wakes at the last resting place.
A room is left by walking, falling or climbing out through an opening at its border.
Screen x increases right and screen y increases down. Each action holds for the requested frames; the game is stopped while the model decides.

disclosure.visibility: geometry mode: the game's collision shapes inside the rectangle of the game plane that the camera shows; nothing outside that rectangle. Occlusion by scenery is NOT applied.
disclosure.geometry: terrain = collision outlines rasterised at 0.5 units and cut into rectangles (top = a surface, bottom = a ceiling); doors, hazards, enemies and the knight = bounds of their colliders; all clipped to the camera rectangle
can_exceed_human_view: collision without art (invisible walls) and openings hidden behind foreground art (secret rooms)
dark rooms are reported like lit rooms
things covered by foreground scenery, fog or particles are reported (no occlusion)
a collider that is active while its sprite is faded out
decoration that looks dangerous is not reported as a hazard
exact collision geometry and hit boxes
